```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6)
library(tidyverse); library(tidytext); library(tm); library(topicmodels)
library(textstem); library(wordcloud); library(RColorBrewer); library(slam)
set.seed(1234)
```

# Question 2.1 - Data frame (file_name, content) and denoising

```{r load}
# Q2.1
unzip("news.zip", exdir = "news", overwrite = TRUE)
files <- list.files("news", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
files <- files[!grepl("(__MACOSX|/\\.)", files)]

news_df <- tibble(
  file_name = basename(files),
  content   = map_chr(files, ~ paste(readLines(.x, warn = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8"), collapse = " "))
)
cat("Documents loaded:", nrow(news_df), "\n")
head(news_df |> mutate(content = substr(content, 1, 120)))
```

The following denoising techniques were applied: transliteration of non-ASCII characters, lower-casing,
removal of URLs, e-mail addresses, HTML tags, numbers and punctuation, whitespace normalisation, removal of
empty and duplicate documents, stop-word removal (standard and domain-specific news words), removal of
tokens shorter than three characters, and lemmatisation.

```{r clean}
# Q2.1
clean_text <- function(x) {
  x |>
    iconv(to = "ASCII//TRANSLIT", sub = " ") |>
    tolower() |>
    str_replace_all("http\\S+|www\\.\\S+|\\S+@\\S+", " ") |>
    str_replace_all("<[^>]+>", " ") |>
    str_replace_all("[0-9]+", " ") |>
    str_replace_all("[[:punct:]]", " ") |>
    str_squish()
}

news_df <- news_df |>
  mutate(clean = clean_text(content)) |>
  filter(nchar(clean) > 50) |>
  distinct(clean, .keep_all = TRUE)

custom_stop <- tibble(word = c("said","say","mr","mrs","also","will","year","new","one","two",
                               "can","just","like","get","told","people"))
tokens <- news_df |>
  unnest_tokens(word, clean) |>
  anti_join(stop_words, by = "word") |>
  anti_join(custom_stop, by = "word") |>
  filter(nchar(word) > 2) |>
  mutate(word = lemmatize_words(word))

cat("Documents after cleaning:", n_distinct(tokens$file_name), " | Tokens:", nrow(tokens), "\n")
tokens |> count(word, sort = TRUE) |> head(15)
```

# Question 2.2 - LDA: top n topics and top k words

## Number of topics

```{r dtm}
# Q2.2
dtm <- tokens |> count(file_name, word) |> cast_dtm(file_name, word, n)
dtm <- removeSparseTerms(dtm, 0.99)
dtm <- dtm[row_sums(dtm) > 0, ]
dtm
```

```{r tune, fig.height=5}
# Q2.2
ks <- 2:8
perp <- sapply(ks, function(k) perplexity(LDA(dtm, k = k, control = list(seed = 1234))))
tune <- tibble(topics = ks, perplexity = perp)
ggplot(tune, aes(topics, perplexity)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue") + geom_point(size = 3, colour = "steelblue") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = ks) +
  labs(title = "Figure 2.1 - Perplexity by number of topics",
       x = "Number of topics (k)", y = "Perplexity (lower is better)") +
  theme_minimal()
tune
```

## LDA model

```{r lda}
# Q2.2
n_topics <- 5
k_words  <- 10

lda <- LDA(dtm, k = n_topics, method = "Gibbs",
           control = list(seed = 1234, iter = 1000, burnin = 200))

beta  <- tidy(lda, matrix = "beta")
gamma <- tidy(lda, matrix = "gamma")

top_terms <- beta |> group_by(topic) |> slice_max(beta, n = k_words, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  arrange(topic, desc(beta)) |> ungroup()
```

## Top k words per topic

```{r topwords}
# Q2.2
top_terms |>
  group_by(topic) |>
  mutate(rank = row_number(), word = paste0(term, " (", round(beta, 3), ")")) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(rank, topic, word) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = topic, values_from = word, names_prefix = "Topic ") |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Top words per topic with beta (word probability) in brackets")
```

## Word distribution per topic

```{r distribution}
# Q2.2
top_terms |> group_by(topic) |>
  summarise(top_k_probability_mass = round(sum(beta), 3),
            words = paste(term, collapse = ", ")) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Share of each topic's probability carried by its top words")

gamma |> group_by(topic) |> summarise(avg_document_share = round(mean(gamma), 3)) |>
  arrange(desc(avg_document_share)) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Topic prevalence across the corpus")
```

## Findings

```{r findings22, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
freq_all <- tokens |> count(word, sort = TRUE)
prev <- gamma |> group_by(topic) |> summarise(share = mean(gamma), .groups = "drop")
dom  <- gamma |> group_by(document) |> slice_max(gamma, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |> count(topic, name = "docs")
tt   <- top_terms |> group_by(topic) |>
  summarise(w = paste(head(term, 5), collapse = ", "), mass = sum(beta), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(prev, by = "topic") |> left_join(dom, by = "topic") |>
  mutate(docs = replace_na(docs, 0L))
best_k <- tune$topics[which.min(tune$perplexity)]
top_prev <- tt |> slice_max(share, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

cat(sprintf("The corpus consists of %d South African news articles. After denoising, %d meaningful tokens remained, ",
            nrow(news_df), nrow(tokens)),
    sprintf("and the most frequent terms were *%s*, which reflects the dominant subject matter of the collection.\n\n",
            paste(sprintf("%s (%d)", head(freq_all$word, 5), head(freq_all$n, 5)), collapse = ", ")))
cat(sprintf("Perplexity was calculated for models with 2 to 8 topics; the lowest perplexity was obtained at k = %d (%.1f). ",
            best_k, min(tune$perplexity)),
    sprintf("A %d-topic model was retained because, for a small corpus of %d articles, it balances statistical fit with topics that remain distinct and interpretable.\n\n",
            n_topics, nrow(news_df)))
cat("The word distribution per topic is summarised below:\n\n")
for (i in seq_len(nrow(tt))) {
  cat(sprintf("* **Topic %d** is characterised by *%s*. Its top %d words carry %.1f%% of the topic's probability mass, the topic accounts for %.1f%% of the corpus on average and it is the dominant topic in %d article(s).\n",
              tt$topic[i], tt$w[i], k_words, 100 * tt$mass[i], 100 * tt$share[i], tt$docs[i]))
}
cat(sprintf("\nTopic %d is the most prevalent theme in the collection (%.1f%% average share), which indicates that it is the subject most frequently reported on in these articles.\n",
            top_prev$topic, 100 * top_prev$share))
```

# Question 2.3 - Visualisations

## Visualisation 1 - Top words per topic

```{r vis1, fig.height=7}
# Q2.3
top_terms |>
  mutate(term = reorder_within(term, beta, topic)) |>
  ggplot(aes(beta, term, fill = factor(topic))) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ topic, scales = "free", labeller = label_both) +
  scale_y_reordered() +
  labs(title = "Top 10 Words per LDA Topic", x = "Beta (probability of word within topic)", y = "Term")
```

## Visualisation 2 - Word cloud per topic

```{r vis2, fig.height=8}
# Q2.3
par(mfrow = c(2, ceiling(n_topics / 2)), mar = c(0, 0, 2, 0))
for (t in seq_len(n_topics)) {
  d <- beta |> filter(topic == t) |> slice_max(beta, n = 40, with_ties = FALSE)
  wordcloud(d$term, d$beta, scale = c(3, 0.5), colors = brewer.pal(8, "Dark2"), random.order = FALSE)
  title(paste("Topic", t))
}
```

## Visualisation 3 - Word-topic heat map

```{r vis3, fig.height=8}
# Q2.3
top_terms |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(topic), reorder(term, beta), fill = beta)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Word-Topic Probability Heat Map", x = "Topic", y = "Term", fill = "Beta")
```

## Findings

```{r findings23, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
lead  <- top_terms |> group_by(topic) |> slice_max(beta, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |> ungroup()
shared <- top_terms |> count(term) |> filter(n > 1)
cat("The bar charts and word clouds show the highest-probability word in each topic: ",
    paste(sprintf("Topic %d - *%s* (beta = %.3f)", lead$topic, lead$term, lead$beta), collapse = "; "),
    ". The larger the bar or the word in the cloud, the more strongly that word defines the topic.\n\n", sep = "")
if (nrow(shared) > 0) {
  cat(sprintf("The heat map shows that %d word(s) (*%s*) rank among the top words of more than one topic, which indicates some overlap between these themes, while the remaining words are specific to a single topic and make the topics clearly distinguishable.\n",
              nrow(shared), paste(head(shared$term, 8), collapse = ", ")))
} else {
  cat("The heat map shows that no word ranks among the top words of more than one topic, which indicates that the topics are clearly separated from one another.\n")
}
```
